method_note: Collected via WebSearch only (direct weather-site fetches blocked). Values 5-10 days out come from search-snippet summaries of extended/long-range model forecasts (world-weather.info, AccuWeather monthly, timeanddate, local TV outlooks) blended with climatology; treat anything beyond ~7 days as low-to-medium confidence. temp_f is a best estimate for kickoff time, not the daily high.
tropical_outlook: Quiet season: 2026 Atlantic has produced only five named storms and zero hurricanes as of Sept 4 (most tranquil since 1941; strong El Nino, dry air and shear suppressing development; NOAA holds a below-normal outlook). Tropical Storm Edouard (5th named storm) made landfall in SW Louisiana near Johnson Bayou on Tue Sept 1 and its remnants dumped 12+ inches on East Texas with major flooding; Houston had a Flood Watch Wed Sept 2-3 and lingering tropical moisture/scattered storms through the Labor Day weekend. As of the latest NHC outlook, no tropical cyclone formation is expected in the Atlantic basin during the next 7 days, though Houston outlets mention a weak area of disturbed weather in the Gulf that may keep rain chances elevated in SE Texas. No system currently threatens Jacksonville, Houston, Charlotte, Tampa or the mid-Atlantic for the Sept 13-14 weekend; residual Gulf moisture is the only tropical-related factor and it mainly affects Houston (roof will be closed anyway) and adds to Jacksonville's normal afternoon-storm risk. Re-check NHC on Sept 10-11.

2026_01_NE_SEA.notes: Wed Sept 9, 5:20pm PT kickoff. Extended forecasts show Wednesday as the warmest day of the stretch (highs 72-77F, dry, light wind); kickoff temp likely upper 60s cooling to low 60s by the 4th quarter. NWS Seattle AFD notes an upper trough over the PNW Fri-Sun Sept 4-6 with showers, then ~55% of ensembles building ridging early next week with model divergence, so a small chance the dry/warm signal erodes. Climatology for Sept 9: high ~72, low ~55, ~20% rain chance, wind 6-8 mph.

2026_01_SF_LA.notes: Fri Sept 11, 10:35am AEST kickoff (Thu Sept 10, 5:35pm PT). MCG is confirmed open-air (Ticketmaster: 'the MCG has an open roof and is considered an outdoor event... weather protection isn't guaranteed'). Extended forecast: cool/showery early in the week, clearing from Wed Sept 9 with winds dropping; Thu 10th high ~16C (61F), Fri 11th high ~19C (66F) and clear, warming further into the weekend. A late-morning kickoff means game temps roughly 12-17C (54-63F). Melbourne September climatology: avg high 17C/63F, low 8-9C/48F, ~10 rain days/month (~29% daily chance), avg wind ~8 mph; spring is the most changeable season so a fast-moving front can still bring a shower.

2026_01_CHI_CAR.notes: Sun Sept 13, 1pm ET. Long-range forecast: clear, high 82F / low 62F. Charlotte just came off a near-record early-September heat wave (mid-upper 90s) that a cold front ends Sept 5-6, with 'back in the 80s but still above average' through the following week. Mid-September climatology: high ~82, low ~62, ~25% daily rain chance, wind 5-7 mph. Low weather impact expected.

2026_01_TB_CIN.conditions: mostly sunny, warm, light SE breeze
2026_01_TB_CIN.notes: Sun Sept 13, 1pm ET. Long-range forecast: mostly sunny, high near 88F, overnight low mid-60s, light SE wind 4-7 mph, no precipitation expected; local outlook headlined 'sunny skies and warm temperatures Sept 8-14'. That runs a few degrees above mid-September climatology (high ~82, low ~58, 23% daily rain chance, avg wind ~9.6 mph), so kickoff estimate blended to ~84F.

2026_01_BUF_HOU.conditions: hot and humid outside; scattered afternoon storms possible; roof almost certainly closed so effectively indoor
2026_01_BUF_HOU.notes: Sun Sept 13, 12pm CT. AccuWeather long-range: high 93F / low 75F; Space City Weather says Sunday is a toss-up between lingering tropical-moisture showers or high pressure clearing things out into the low-mid 90s, and no meaningful cold front shows up through mid-September. Texans policy is to consider opening the roof only when game-time temp is projected 50-80F with no rain threat; they have essentially never opened it for a September day game, and the outside forecast (90s, humid, storm chance) makes a closed roof a near-certainty. Treat as dome conditions (no wind/heat effect on play). Edouard remnants caused flooding in E Texas Sept 1-3 but should be long gone by game day.

2026_01_BAL_IND.roof: retractable (status uncertain; lean CLOSED if heat persists)
2026_01_BAL_IND.conditions: hot, mostly sunny; showers possible by evening
2026_01_BAL_IND.notes: Sun Sept 13, 1pm ET. One long-range model (world-weather.info) shows Sept 13 as the hottest day of its 16-day window at 97F with NW wind and showers arriving that evening, then rain Monday morning; that is extreme vs climatology (high ~80, low ~58) and should be discounted. Local outlets (WISH-TV, Sept 3) describe a heat wave ending with a Sept 5-6 front, mid-80s for Labor Day, then heat rebuilding to ~90 by mid-next-week. Best estimate: upper 80s to ~90 at kickoff, low rain risk during the game, front approaching afterward. Roof: Colts keep it closed below 40F and can only close mid-game for rain; they opened it for the 2024 opener in pleasant weather but have kept it closed for heat/'operational issues' before. Roof status is announced game-day on @ColtsLife; with upper-80s/90 temps a closed roof is somewhat more likely than open. If open, wind impact minimal (~8 mph).

2026_01_CLE_JAX.conditions: hot and humid (heat index 100+), afternoon thunderstorms likely
2026_01_CLE_JAX.notes: Sun Sept 13, 1pm ET. Long-range forecast: high ~95F with another risk of afternoon thunderstorms, winds calming that night. Action News Jax describes a very hot stretch (mid-upper 90s, heat index 100-105) with scattered afternoon/evening storms daily fed by Gulf moisture; the pattern is expected to persist. Kickoff temp near 90-92 with typical 1-4pm storm timing overlapping the game; lightning delays are a real possibility (~1-in-3 in this pattern). Sept climatology: high ~87, low ~70, ~45% daily rain chance, wind 7-9 mph (sea breeze). No tropical system threatens the area.

2026_01_ATL_PIT.conditions: partly cloudy, warm and humid (climatology, nudged warm)
2026_01_ATL_PIT.notes: Sun Sept 13, 1pm ET. No specific point forecast for Sept 13 surfaced (NWS/local forecasts run through ~Sept 10). Mid-September climatology: high ~75F, low ~58F, avg wind 8.5 mph, ~28% daily rain chance, cloudy ~36% of the time. Local outlets say heat and humidity 'spike over the next week' after Labor Day with long-range highs up to ~90, so the estimate is nudged to ~80F at kickoff. Neighboring Cincinnati long-range is sunny/upper 80s the same day, suggesting a warm, mostly dry ridge over the Ohio Valley.

2026_01_NYJ_TEN.conditions: morning clouds clearing, hot afternoon; rain arriving Sunday night after the game
2026_01_NYJ_TEN.notes: Sun Sept 13, 12pm CT. Long-range forecast: clouds in the morning clearing by afternoon, high near 92F, then moderate rain Sunday night with lows ~71F. Local outlets note rain chances stay low then return 'next week' as fronts become more frequent. Game window (noon-3pm) should be dry but hot/humid; a front-driven rain risk is mostly post-game, but timing errors of several hours at this range mean a ~20% chance of showers reaching the 4th quarter. Sept climatology: high ~85, low ~62, ~8 rain days/month, wind 5-7 mph.

2026_01_DEN_KC.conditions: partly cloudy, warm evening, breezy; thunderstorm chance (climatology)
2026_01_DEN_KC.notes: Mon Sept 14, 7:15pm CT. No reliable point forecast for Sept 14 surfaced (KSHB/NWS run through ~Sept 10). Mid-September climatology: high ~83F, low ~65F, avg wind ~14 mph (windiest of the Week 1 outdoor venues), ~22% daily rain chance (~10 rain days/month, 4.5 in). KC has been in a historic heat wave since Aug 29 (hottest opening nine days of September since 1947 if it holds through Sept 9), and NWS mentioned below-normal temperatures for the following week, implying a front passes between Sept 9 and 14; that transition makes a storm chance around Sept 14 plausible, but timing is unknowable at this range. Some undated aggregator snippets about 'Monday storms / enhanced severe risk' in KC appear to be from other years and were disregarded. Wind is the main variable to re-check closer to game day.
